lines: Teaching, assessing and tracking learning, in one place.
Courses, exams, discussion, curriculum plans and an adaptive learning engine, in one K-12 module.
One set of records, so teachers need not rebuild the picture by hand each term.

problem.label: An illustration, not your school
beats: It is Sunday evening and you are building next week's lessons from three different folders.
Last term's question bank is in one file, the exam blueprint in another, the lesson plan in a notebook.
Marking is on paper, so you chase submissions and compile results by hand.
Then someone asks who is falling behind, and you start the picture again from scratch.
problem.turn: Scholar Learn keeps content, exams, lesson plans and progress in one place.

intelligence.lead: Scholar Learn reads how the curriculum and the class's work connect, and shows which concept comes first and what practice step is next.

modules.basis: Knowledge graph of concepts and prerequisites
modules.asks: Which concept must be learned before this one?
What should this student practise next?
How did each class do in its exams?
What was delivered, and what was assessed?

intelligence.close: Rules decide each step. Teachers decide what to do.

ai.lead: AI assists staff with drafts and wording. Rules, not AI, decide each learning step.

uses.name: Question generation
uses.line: Generates questions by Bloom level, showing options and the correct answer.

uses.name: Concept links
uses.line: Suggests concept tags and prerequisite links, marked as drafts until staff approve.

uses.name: Report summaries
uses.line: Writes short report summaries from recorded figures only.

uses.name: Next-step wording
uses.line: Rules decide each learning step; AI only phrases it.

uses.name: Form text
uses.line: Drafts text in forms such as homework and exam instructions.

ai.guard: Text in a form waits for Apply. Suggested tags and links stay drafts until staff approve.
ai.control: School administrators set AI policies, prompts and guardrails.

sample.label: Sample draft. Illustrative.
sample.text: Homework: Read chapter 4 and solve exercises 1 to 5. Write two sentences about the main idea. Submit by Friday.

items.text: Bloom's revised taxonomy interrelates knowledge with cognitive processes; Webb's Depth of Knowledge communicates the content complexity of learning expectations and assessment items.
items.source: Anderson, Krathwohl and others, Pearson; Norman Webb, WebbAlign

items.text: CASEL's framework, the CASEL Wheel, positions social and emotional competencies within classroom, school, family and community settings.
The Next Generation Science Standards are K-12 science standards created through a state-led process and based on the Framework for K-12 Science Education.
items.source: Achieve, Next Generation Science Standards, achieve.org

items.text: The National Career Development Guidelines are a framework of career development competencies and indicators of mastery, maintained by the National Career Development Association.
items.source: National Career Development Association, NCDG Framework, ncda.org

items.text: NCERT publishes the National Curriculum Framework for School Education and, separately, class-wise Learning Outcomes at the Elementary Stage.
items.source: NCERT, NCF for School Education 2023; Learning Outcomes at the Elementary Stage

Month and period plans, with delivered and assessed outcomes.
Set, collect and mark work; build papers and see results.

How concepts connect through prerequisites, down to single concepts.

Raise a doubt by subject and chapter, and read replies in a thread.
Submit your own homework and assignments.

benefits: See the curriculum by subject and month, with NCF goals.
See exam results across the institute.
Set AI policies, prompts and guardrails for adaptive learning.

notes.summary: Let the three lines land one at a time. Ask: where does your teachers' work live today, and how many places is that?
notes.problem: Tell it as their Sunday evening, not ours. Pause after 'start the picture again from scratch'. Say it is an illustration, not their school.
notes.intelligence: These are questions the school's own records answer, not predictions and not AI. Rules choose the practice step; the teacher decides what to do. If asked how the rules work: a student skips what they already know, a missing prerequisite is repaired first, and earlier work is rechecked after a few days.
notes.ai: Say exactly what is true. Text typed into a form waits for Apply and then Save. Suggested concept tags and prerequisite links stay drafts until staff approve or reject them. Do NOT say AI-generated questions wait for approval: they are saved straight away and staff can hold them. Rules, not AI, choose each learning step; AI only phrases it. If asked about control: school administrators set AI policies, prompts and guardrails in the learning-engine administration.
notes.research: Say what each source is, not what it proves. Bloom and the NCF/NCERT outcomes shaped the content; CASEL, NGSS and NCDG are used as tag vocabularies for framework views, not as full coverage (NGSS: the science and engineering practices only; CASEL: self-awareness is left unmapped on purpose). Do not say Scholar Learn conforms to, is assessed by, or is endorsed by any of them. No figures are shown; if asked for numbers, say none are claimed.
notes.features: Two groups. Let them point at the group their work is in, then open that screen. Do not read the lines.
notes.roles: Let the client name their own role first, then open it. Every use line is an illustration. School leaders is inferred from the admin tier: confirm before using it. There is no academic-coordinator role and no parent view of Learn.
